# Claude Code Plugin Structure Spec

## Directory Layout

Every Claude Code plugin must follow this layout:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json          # REQUIRED manifest
├── agents/
│   └── audit-trail-agent.md # REQUIRED — injected by agent-builder from ai-baseline
├── skills/
│   └── baseline-enforcer.md # REQUIRED — injected by agent-builder from ai-baseline
├── commands/                # optional — slash command files
└── README.md                # REQUIRED for marketplace submission
```

## Baseline Requirement

Every plugin generated by agent-builder must include:

- `skills/baseline-enforcer.md` — copied verbatim from `ai-baseline/skills/baseline-enforcer.md`
- `agents/audit-trail-agent.md` — copied verbatim from `ai-baseline/agents/audit-trail-agent.md`
- `requires: ai-baseline` in README under `## Dependencies`
- `Import the baseline-enforcer skill at session start and before any output or Opus call.` in the primary agent's preamble

Omitting any of these is a spec violation. The auditor-agent must flag missing baseline components as errors (not warnings).

## plugin.json Fields

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | string | Unique plugin identifier, kebab-case |
| `version` | yes | string | Semver (e.g., "1.0.0") |
| `description` | yes | string | One-sentence user-facing description |
| `category` | yes | string | One of: development, productivity, language, data, security, other |
| `author` | yes | object | `{ "name": "...", "email": "..." }` |
| `homepage` | no | string | URL to plugin homepage or repo |
| `license` | no | string | SPDX license identifier |
| `keywords` | no | string[] | Discovery tags |

## Agent File Format (`agents/*.md`)

```markdown
---
name: agent-name            # kebab-case, unique within plugin
description: |              # trigger phrase — when should this agent be used?
  Use this agent when X. Triggers on Y.
model: sonnet               # haiku | sonnet | opus (omit to inherit user default)
---

[System prompt body — describes role, inputs, outputs, constraints]
```

**Rules for agents:**
- One concern per agent. If you can't describe what it does in one sentence, split it.
- Declare tool needs in the system prompt body under a `## Tools` section.
- The `description` field is what Claude Code uses to decide when to invoke the agent.
- Never spawn unbounded subagent trees — every Agent tool call must have a defined exit condition.
- Agents must not write to disk unless they are explicitly the "write" step in a pipeline.

## Skill File Format (`skills/*.md` or `SKILL.md`)

```markdown
---
name: skill-name            # kebab-case, unique within plugin
description: |              # one line — when to invoke this skill
  Use when X, before doing Y.
---

# Skill Title

[Skill body — reusable technique, pattern, or reference guide]
```

**Rules for skills:**
- Skills must have at least one hard gate: a `DO NOT` or `STOP` rule.
- Skills must have an unambiguous trigger condition in the `description` field.
- Skills are reference guides, not narratives. Write for a cold agent with no prior context.

## Command File Format (`commands/*.md`)

```markdown
---
description: One-line description of what this command does
argument-hint: [optional-arg]    # shown in autocomplete
---

[System prompt — instructions Claude follows when this slash command is invoked]
```

## Marketplace Submission Requirements

Before publishing to a marketplace:
- `README.md` must exist and describe installation, usage, and at least one example
- `plugin.json` must have `name`, `version`, `description`, `category`, `author`
- All agent files must have `name` and `description` in frontmatter
- All skill files must have `name` and `description` in frontmatter
- No agent may request tool permissions broader than its stated purpose
